name: Santuario de la Virgen de la Cabeza (1936–37 siege), Andújar
story: In September 1936 about 250 Civil Guards, some Falangists and around 1,000 of their family members and civilians from Jaén province shut themselves into this hilltop sanctuary in the Sierra Morena, deep inside Republican territory. Captain Santiago Cortés deposed the commander who favoured surrender and held out for more than seven months, supplied by Nationalist aircraft dropping food and medicine. A Nationalist relief offensive stalled at Lopera in December. Republican forces under Lt. Col. García Vallejo and Maj. Martínez Cartón, eventually 6,000 or more men, stormed the ruins on 1 May 1937; Cortés was mortally wounded and the survivors surrendered. Franco's regime made the siege a heroic legend, rather like the Alcázar of Toledo.
see: The sanctuary, rebuilt after its destruction in the siege, on its granite hilltop; a 22 m monument of 1965 with a bronze Angel of Victory lifting a fallen defender; relics including Cortés's Laureate Cross.
plan: Open daily as a working shrine; 32 km north of Andújar by the A-6177 through the Sierra de Andújar park. Avoid the huge Romería on the last weekend of April unless you want the pilgrimage.

boxes.text: The monument and its inscriptions reflect the Francoist narrative and are debated under Spain's democratic memory laws. Numbers of besiegers are given as 6,000–12,000.
